rules.reason: git checkout can destructively overwrite uncommitted changes you may have forgotten about
rules.guidance: Use 'git switch <branch>' for branches. Use 'git diff <file>' to see what changed before discarding.

rules.reason: git restore can destructively overwrite uncommitted changes you may have forgotten about
rules.guidance: Use 'git diff <file>' to see what changed first. If you truly need to discard changes, confirm with the user before proceeding.

rules.reason: Recursive delete of root directory is not allowed
rules.guidance: Use specific paths like ./directory instead of absolute paths from root

rules.reason: Recursive delete of home directory is not allowed
rules.guidance: Use specific paths within your project directory

rules.reason: Force push can overwrite remote history and affect collaborators
rules.guidance: Consider using --force-with-lease for safer force pushes

rules.reason: Hard reset discards all uncommitted changes permanently
rules.guidance: Use 'git reset --soft' to keep changes staged. Never use --hard without explicit user approval.

rules.reason: chmod 777 grants overly permissive file permissions (world-writable)
rules.guidance: Use more restrictive permissions like 755 for directories or 644 for files

rules.reason: Writing directly to disk device will destroy data
rules.guidance: Never write directly to /dev/sd* devices

rules.reason: Environment files often contain secrets and API keys
rules.guidance: Review the content carefully before allowing access

rules.reason: PEM files contain private keys and certificates
rules.guidance: Private keys should never be read or modified by AI agents

rules.reason: SSH private keys must remain confidential
rules.guidance: Never expose SSH private keys to any external system

rules.reason: SSH directory contains private keys and sensitive configuration
rules.guidance: Only allow access if absolutely necessary for SSH configuration

rules.reason: GPG directory contains encryption keys
rules.guidance: GPG keys are sensitive - only allow if needed for signing operations

rules.reason: AWS credentials file contains access keys
rules.guidance: Use IAM roles or environment variables instead of credential files

rules.reason: Git credentials file contains authentication tokens
rules.guidance: Use SSH keys or credential helpers instead

rules.reason: Netrc file contains login credentials for network services
rules.guidance: Never expose network credentials to AI agents

rules.reason: Docker config may contain registry authentication
rules.guidance: Review if registry credentials are present before allowing

rules.reason: Kubernetes config contains cluster access credentials
rules.guidance: Only allow if needed for Kubernetes operations

rules.reason: NPM config may contain authentication tokens
rules.guidance: Review if auth tokens are present before allowing

rules.reason: Shell history may contain sensitive commands and secrets
rules.guidance: Shell history should remain private

rules.reason: System authentication files are restricted
rules.guidance: Never allow access to system authentication files

rules.reason: Recursive force delete can remove important files
rules.guidance: Verify the path before allowing recursive deletion

rules.reason: Commits create permanent history entries that may be difficult to undo
rules.guidance: Review staged changes with 'git diff --cached' before committing. Ensure commit message is appropriate.

rules.reason: Revert creates a new commit that undoes previous changes
rules.guidance: Verify which commit is being reverted and understand its impact on the codebase.

rules.reason: git clean permanently removes untracked files that cannot be recovered
rules.guidance: Use 'git clean -n' (dry-run) first to see what will be deleted. Untracked files are not in git history.

rules.reason: git stash manipulates the working tree and index behind the user's back. Agents must never touch git stash.
rules.guidance: Do not use git stash for any reason. If you need to compare before/after, use git diff. If you need a clean tree, ask the user.

rules.reason: Deleting branches removes references to commits which may become unreachable
rules.guidance: Ensure the branch has been merged or its changes are no longer needed. Use -d (safe) instead of -D (force) when possible.

rules.reason: Deleting tags removes version markers that may be referenced by releases
rules.guidance: Verify the tag is not associated with a published release before deleting.

rules.reason: Deleting remote branches or tags affects all collaborators
rules.guidance: Ensure no one else is working on the branch and it has been merged if needed.

rules.reason: Rebase rewrites commit history which can cause issues if commits were already pushed
rules.guidance: Never rebase commits that have been pushed to a shared repository. Use 'git merge' for shared branches.

rules.reason: Cherry-pick copies commits which can create duplicate changes in history
rules.guidance: Understand why the commit is being cherry-picked and consider if merge would be more appropriate.

rules.reason: Merge combines branches and creates merge commits that affect history
rules.guidance: Review the changes being merged with 'git diff' and resolve any conflicts carefully.

rules.reason: git am applies patches as commits, modifying repository history
rules.guidance: Review the patch content before applying. Use --dry-run to test first.

rules.reason: Direct access to work-units.json bypasses fspec workflow rules and can corrupt work unit state.
rules.guidance: Use the Fspec tool instead: 'list-work-units' to browse, 'show-work-unit' to inspect, and 'update-work-unit' or 'update-work-unit-status' to modify work units. Do not read or edit spec/work-units.json directly.

rules.reason: Direct access to tags.json bypasses fspec tag validation and registration workflows.
rules.guidance: Use the Fspec tool instead: 'list-tags' to inspect tags, 'register-tag' to add tags, and 'add-tag-to-feature' or 'add-tag-to-scenario' to apply them. Do not read or edit spec/tags.json directly.

rules.reason: Do NOT pipe cargo test output through head/tail/grep. Tests are expensive to run — re-running them just to see a different slice of the output is wasteful and slow.
rules.guidance: Tee the output to a file and then read it: 'cargo test ... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-output.txt' then use the Read tool on /tmp/test-output.txt. This way you run the tests ONCE and can inspect the full output as many times as needed.

rules.reason: Do NOT pipe npm test output through head/tail/grep. Tests are expensive to run — re-running them just to see a different slice of the output is wasteful and slow.
rules.guidance: Tee the output to a file and then read it: 'npm test 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-output.txt' then use the Read tool on /tmp/test-output.txt. This way you run the tests ONCE and can inspect the full output as many times as needed.

rules.reason: Do NOT pipe vitest output through head/tail/grep. Tests are expensive to run — re-running them just to see a different slice of the output is wasteful and slow.
rules.guidance: Tee the output to a file and then read it: 'vitest ... 2>&1 | tee /tmp/test-output.txt' then use the Read tool on /tmp/test-output.txt. This way you run the tests ONCE and can inspect the full output as many times as needed.

rules.reason: The h2_database directory contains database files that must not be read, modified, or deleted without caution
rules.guidance: Use application-level database tools or queries instead of direct file access. Only access if you need to debug database issues.

rules.reason: Direct access to foundation.json bypasses fspec foundation management and can corrupt project state.
rules.guidance: Use the Fspec tool instead: 'show-foundation' to view, and use 'update-foundation' with section names to modify. Do not read or edit spec/foundation.json directly.

rules.reason: Do NOT use 'grep -rn' / 'grep -r' via Bash. Recursive grep is slow, doesn't respect .gitignore, and floods the context with output.
rules.guidance: Use the Grep tool instead — it uses ripgrep under the hood, respects .gitignore, is faster, and supports glob/type filters and output modes. Example: Grep(pattern='foo', glob='*.rs', output_mode='content').

rules.reason: YOU MUST USE THE FSPEC TOOL
rules.guidance: Use the Fspec tool for all fspec operations. Do NOT run fspec CLI commands via Bash.

rules.reason: YOU MUST USE THE FSPEC TOOL
rules.guidance: Use the Fspec tool for all fspec operations. Do NOT invoke 'fspec && ./dist/index.js' via Bash.

rules.reason: Running http-server in the background with & can hang the agent loop
rules.guidance: Use GNU screen to run http-server: 'screen -dmS <session-name> npx http-server <options>'. This properly manages the process and prevents hanging the agent loop.

rules.reason: Unscoped workspace test runs can compile hundreds of large binaries with full debug info, fill the disk, and crash the machine. Previously caused a 300 GB target/ directory and a mid-link crash.
rules.guidance: Scope the run by package and target: 'cargo test -p <crate> --test <name>'. For broader runs, list packages explicitly and drop debug info: 'CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 cargo test -p <a> -p <b> -j 12'. Tee long output to a file instead of re-running.

rules.reason: A bare 'cargo test' run from a workspace root is equivalent to --workspace: it tests EVERY member crate. This has previously compiled hundreds of multi-GB test binaries, filled the disk and crashed the machine.
rules.guidance: Only proceed if the current directory is a single small crate, NOT a workspace root. Otherwise scope the run: 'cargo test -p <crate> [--test <name>]', optionally with CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0.

rules.reason: Recursive delete of the system drive root is not allowed
rules.guidance: Use specific subdirectory paths like C:\Users\<username>\project instead of the drive root

rules.reason: Recursive delete of the user home directory is not allowed
rules.guidance: Use specific paths within your project directory

rules.reason: Recursive force delete (rmdir /s /q) can remove important files and directories
rules.guidance: Verify the target path before allowing recursive deletion. Use 'dir <path>' first to confirm what will be deleted.

rules.reason: Recursive force delete (del /s /q) can remove important files
rules.guidance: Verify the target path and file patterns before allowing recursive deletion. Use 'dir <path>' first to confirm what will be deleted.

rules.reason: PowerShell Remove-Item -Recurse -Force can remove important files and directories
rules.guidance: Verify the target path before allowing recursive deletion. Use 'Get-ChildItem <path>' first to confirm what will be deleted.

rules.reason: Recursive delete of the system drive root via PowerShell is not allowed
rules.guidance: Use specific subdirectory paths instead of the drive root

rules.reason: Formatting a disk volume destroys all data on that partition
rules.guidance: Never format system or data drives. If formatting a USB/removable drive is truly needed, confirm with the user first.

rules.reason: diskpart 'clean' command wipes all partitions and data from a disk
rules.guidance: Never use diskpart clean. If disk management is needed, use 'diskpart list disk' to inspect first and confirm with the user.

rules.reason: Clear-Disk PowerShell cmdlet wipes all partitions and data from a disk
rules.guidance: Never use Clear-Disk. If disk management is needed, use 'Get-PhysicalDisk' to inspect first and confirm with the user.

rules.reason: Format-Volume PowerShell cmdlet formats a volume and destroys all data
rules.guidance: Never use Format-Volume. If volume management is needed, use 'Get-Volume' to inspect first and confirm with the user.

rules.reason: Windows system configuration files (SAM, SYSTEM, SECURITY, SOFTWARE) contain authentication data and system settings
rules.guidance: Never allow access to Windows system configuration files. Use 'reg query' for specific registry lookups if needed.

rules.reason: cmdkey manages Windows stored credentials (passwords, tokens) which must remain confidential
rules.guidance: Never list or manipulate Windows stored credentials. Use application-specific credential managers instead.

rules.reason: PowerShell history may contain sensitive commands, credentials, and secrets
rules.guidance: Shell history should remain private. Do not read or export PowerShell history.

rules.reason: Running processes in the background with 'start /b' can hang the agent loop
rules.guidance: Use 'Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden <command>' in PowerShell, or run the process in a dedicated terminal session.

rules.reason: Running processes hidden via Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden can hang the agent loop and hide errors
rules.guidance: Run processes in the foreground or use a dedicated terminal. If a background process is truly needed, use 'Start-Process -PassThru' and track the PID.

rules.reason: Granting Full Control (F) via icacls can make files accessible to unauthorized users
rules.guidance: Use more restrictive permissions like 'R' (Read) or 'M' (Modify) instead of 'F' (Full Control) unless explicitly required.

rules.reason: Windows SSH directory contains private keys and sensitive configuration
rules.guidance: Only allow access if absolutely necessary for SSH configuration

rules.reason: AWS credentials file on Windows contains access keys
rules.guidance: Use IAM roles or environment variables instead of credential files

rules.reason: Git credentials file on Windows contains authentication tokens
rules.guidance: Use SSH keys or credential helpers instead

rules.reason: NPM config on Windows may contain authentication tokens
rules.guidance: Review if auth tokens are present before allowing

rules.reason: Deleting registry keys under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE affects the entire system and can cause instability
rules.guidance: Never delete HKLM registry keys. Use 'reg query' to inspect first. If a specific key must be removed, confirm with the user and use 'reg delete' with a specific key path.

rules.reason: Deleting registry keys under HKEY_CURRENT_USER can affect user settings and application behavior
rules.guidance: Use 'reg query' to inspect the key and its subkeys before deleting. Confirm with the user which specific key is being removed.
